ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, transistor T is an NPN bias circuit in a common-emitter form; the collector goes upward through Rc to +Vcc, the emitter goes downward through Re to ground, the base is connected from the left through Rb to the upper power-supply node, and there is also a bypass capacitor Ce beside the emitter. Then reason: The given DC voltages are VB = 3 V, VC = 5 V, VE = 2.3 V. Calculate the base-emitter voltage VBE = VB - VE = 3 - 2.3 = 0.7 V, which for a silicon NPN transistor indicates that the BE junction is forward biased. Also because VC = 5 V is greater than VB = 3 V, the collector-base junction is reverse biased. When the BE junction is forward biased and the CB junction is reverse biased, an NPN silicon transistor operates in the amplification region/active region.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: transistor T is in a common-emitter NPN-style bias circuit with collector upward through Rc to +Vcc, emitter downward through Re to ground, and base at the left through Rb. From the text, use VB = 3 V, VC = 5 V, and VE = 2.3 V. Compute VBE = VB - VE = 0.7 V, so the base-emitter junction is forward biased for silicon. Also VC > VB, so the collector-base junction is reverse biased. A silicon NPN transistor with BE forward biased and CB reverse biased is in the active region.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure and terminal roles: the collector is connected through Rc to the positive supply, the emitter is connected to ground through Re, and the base is biased through Rb, so use NPN operating-region criteria.
